text:
nora: Brain-dump: we need a durable model for API key ownership that supports cross-org keys, rotation automation, and clear RBAC. proposing: introduce `custodian` (team or service principal), `sensitivity` label (LOW/MED/HIGH), and optional `delegated_agents`. thoughts?
ben: +1 to custodian + sensitivity. sensitivity drives rotation cadence and who can view the plaintext. HIGH keys require vault/HSM read gate.
alejandra: Important: delegated_agents are needed for ops automation (helm charts, pipelines). but delegation should be explicit and auditable.
trent: Can we also add `display_name` and `in_use_by` snapshot so UI shows where keys are referenced? That helps owners decide rotation timing.
nora: yep. UI will show a "last-seen" fingerprint from auth logs. we'll need a background job to map references (k8s secrets, infra configs) to keys.
ben: RBAC: actions = {view_metadata, view_secret, rotate, transfer, revoke}. default: custodian+security-admin can do all; delegated_agents can rotate but not transfer.
alejandra: For cross-org infra keys (billing hooks, provider integrations) create special custodian type `GLOBAL_CUSTODIAN` and require two-person approval for transfer or revoke. document list of teams eligible.
trent: Migration path? suggest 3-phase: 1) annotate keys with inferred custodian via heuristics (git owner, last committer, project owner), mark as `INFERRED` 2) notify teams and accept claims 3) enforce custodian required and block new legacy keys.
nora: We'll emit an event for each inferred assignment so audit tooling can replay. Also add `legacy_flag=true` for backwards compat.
ben: Rotation model: allow scheduled rotations (cron-like) for delegated agents, immediate rotate for owners, and emergency rotate API (requires `incident_id` and security-admin). emergency rotate should create a short-lived rollback token valid 30m.
rotate-bot: automation note: can implement rotate flows via /rotate-key <key-id> --reason "incident-123" --force; will create audit entry and send a webhook.
alejandra: How do we prevent accidental transfer abuse? UI should require current owner sign-off (email confirmation) plus an audit record. For programmatic transfers, require a signed approval artifact.
nora: Good. Also include `sensitivity` enforcement: HIGH keys cannot be transferred without security-admin co-approval and must live in HSM-backed vault.
ben: DB change: add columns `custodian_type`, `custodian_id`, `sensitivity`, `delegated_agents` (jsonb list), `owner_state` (INFERRED|CLAIMED|VERIFIED). Migration script template: ```UPDATE api_keys SET owner_state='INFERRED' WHERE custodian_id IS NULL;```
trent: Ops runbook: when rotating keys tied to multi-env infra, do canary rollout: rotate in staging, verify auth success rate > 99.9% for 10m, then roll to prod. add metrics: auth_error_rate, rotation_failures.
nora: Security ops: add a weekly report of keys with sensitivity=HIGH lacking HSM storage. auto-create tickets for remediation.
alejandra: Tests: policy unit tests for RBAC matrix, migration dry-run on snapshot, UI e2e for transfer confirm modal.
nora: Backwards compat: read order for owner: custodian -> inferred owner -> legacy project. Mark inferred with TTL 14d; after TTL escalate to team email.
nora: small nit: log format for audit webhook should include old_owner, new_owner, changed_by, change_reason, and optional incident_id.
ben: I'll draft a tiny RFC follow-up with DB patch, API endpoints (/keys/:id/transfer, /keys/:id/rotate, /keys/search?orphaned=true), and UI mockups. want reviewers: @alejandra @trent.
trent: can we also add a metric to track time-to-claim for inferred keys? helps measure friction.
nora: yes. timeline proposal: day0: migration dry-run, day3: enable inferred annotations + notifications, day10: placeholder assignment + 14d claim window, day25: enforce custodian requirement.
nora: audit-bot: RFC-followup ticket created: SEC-KEY-2026. webhook posted to #audit.
nora: thanks everyone. i'll post the follow-up RFC with migration SQL + runbook and ping for quick reviews.
